deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from fol. 6r, 'Ungleichheiten'): a real number alpha is identified with a cut (A1, A2) of the rationals Q, and beta with a cut (B1, B2). Rational cuts that differ only in where the boundary rational is placed count as 'not essentially different'. Definition: if the cuts are essentially different and A1 ⊆ B1, then alpha < beta. Otherwise alpha > beta.

(1) End of the proof of: if alpha > beta then beta < alpha (begun on the previous page).
- Assume alpha > beta, so A1 is not a subset of B1. Then there is a rational a1' in A1 with a1' not in B1, hence a1' in B2.
- Every b1 is smaller than every b2, and a1' is one of the b2. So b1 < a1' for every b1.
- Every a2 > a1', because a1' is in A1. So no b1 can lie in A2 [justification: b1 < a1' < every a2]. Since (A1, A2) partitions Q, every b1 lies in A1, i.e. B1 ⊆ A1.
- The cuts are essentially different by hypothesis, so beta < alpha by definition.

(2) Satz (continuity, i.e. Dedekind completeness of the reals).
- Statement: suppose the set R of all rational and irrational numbers splits into two classes 𝔄1, 𝔄2 such that every alpha1 in 𝔄1 is smaller than every alpha2 in 𝔄2. Then there exists exactly one number alpha with alpha1 ≤ alpha ≤ alpha2 for all alpha1 in 𝔄1 and all alpha2 in 𝔄2.
- Proof as written: put A1 = 𝔄1 ∩ Q and A2 = 𝔄2 ∩ Q. Then every a1 < a2, so (A1, A2) is a cut of Q. Let alpha be the (rational or irrational) number corresponding to it. The text then asserts that alpha has the required properties.
- It finally notes the two cases. If alpha ∈ 𝔄1, then alpha1 ≤ alpha < alpha2 for all members. If alpha ∈ 𝔄2, then alpha1 < alpha ≤ alpha2.
- Missing steps [my reconstruction, not on the page]:
  (a) A1 and A2 are both nonempty. This needs 𝔄1, 𝔄2 nonempty and the existence of rationals below and above any real.
  (b) Suppose some alpha1 > alpha. Pick a rational c with alpha < c < alpha1 (density lemma). Then c < alpha1 < every alpha2, so c ∉ 𝔄2, hence c ∈ 𝔄1 ∩ Q = A1. But every element of A1 is ≤ alpha, contradicting c > alpha. The symmetric argument gives alpha2 ≥ alpha.
  (c) Uniqueness: if alpha < beta both had the property, take rationals alpha < c < c' < beta. Then c' ∈ 𝔄1 because c' < beta ≤ every alpha2 in the strict sense needed. Also c ∈ 𝔄2 because c > alpha ≥ every alpha1. This gives c ∈ 𝔄2, c' ∈ 𝔄1 with c < c', a contradiction.

(3) Definition: alpha is positive iff alpha > 0, negative iff alpha < 0.

(4) Satz (right-hand column, stated without proof): if alpha > beta and beta > gamma, then alpha > gamma. Proof sketch [mine]: C1 ⊆ B1 ⊆ A1 gives C1 ⊆ A1. Essential difference follows because if C1 and A1 were essentially equal, B1 would be squeezed between them, forcing the cuts of beta and gamma (or alpha and beta) to be essentially equal.

The page is the order-theoretic part (§5 'Ungleichheiten') of a draft of 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen'. It is followed by §6 Addition.
errors: No outright mathematical errors. In (1) the step from b1 < a1' to b1 ∈ A1 is correct but uses that (A1, A2) exhausts Q; this is stated only implicitly via 'weil jede Zahl a2 > a1' ist'.

In the continuity theorem the key claim that alpha satisfies alpha1 ≤ alpha ≤ alpha2 is asserted ('hat die obigen Eigenschaften') rather than proved. The needed lemma, that between two distinct reals lies a rational, is neither proved nor cited on this page. In the 1872 publication the corresponding proof explicitly uses this density property.
Uniqueness ('eine und nur eine') is not proved on the page.
Nonemptiness of 𝔄1, 𝔄2 is not stated as a hypothesis. It is needed for A1, A2 to form a genuine cut.
Transitivity of < is stated without proof.
The equivalence between the case split at the end (alpha in 𝔄1 or in 𝔄2) and the conditions is fine, but the case split does not substitute for the missing argument.

results.what: If alpha > beta then beta < alpha, for the cut-based order (trichotomy/antisymmetry part).
results.modern_name: Linear (total) order on Dedekind cuts; trichotomy

results.what: Every partition of R into a lower class and an upper class is produced by exactly one real number. Proof by restricting the partition to the rationals.
results.modern_name: Dedekind completeness / continuity of the real line (Dedekind's continuity theorem)
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind 1872 (Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen §5, IV); conceived 1858

results.what: Definition of positive and negative reals via comparison with 0.

results.modern_name: Transitivity of the order on Dedekind cuts

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of material published nearly verbatim in Dedekind's 1872 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen' (§5, items II–IV). The continuity theorem's wording matches the published one almost word for word. Only minor drafting details are of interest, such as the explicit 'not essentially different' rational cuts, the gap in the proof here, and the separate section on inequalities preceding addition.

checkable.asserts: For alpha = sqrt(2) as a cut, 7/5 lies in A1 and 3/2 in A2 (A1 = {q : q<0 or q**2<2}).

checkable.sympy: all((q < sqrt(2)) for q in [Rational(k,10) for k in range(-30,15)] if q < Rational(7,5))
checkable.asserts: Finite check of B1 ⊆ A1 for beta = 7/5 < alpha = sqrt(2): every rational below 7/5 is below sqrt(2).
Density example: a rational lies strictly between the distinct reals 7/5 and sqrt(2), as the missing lemma in the continuity proof requires.
Instance of transitivity: sqrt(3) > sqrt(2) > 7/5 implies sqrt(3) > 7/5.
